{"id":"jmap-chat-spec-jou9","title":"Write ToIP mapping guide (jmap-toip-mapping-guide.md)","description":"Non-normative guide mapping the JMAP corpus onto the Trust over IP stack. ToIP is governance/trust framework, not wire protocol, so it lives in a guide, never a draft; drafts gain no ToIP text or requirements.

First step: verify the CURRENT ToIP model (layer names changed across revisions; older 4-layer model vs Technology Architecture Spec). Cite a stable ToIP document.

Sections:
1. Scope disclaimer: non-normative, no new requirements, nothing in JMAP depends on ToIP.
2. Layer mapping table: trust support (DID methods webvh/key/plc, resolver, keyCustody); trust spanning (peer signing keys + DID-bound check; state JMAP federation is parallel to ToIP TSP, not built on it, because JMAP is HTTP client/server sync, not a peer messaging substrate); trust tasks (MIMI/MLS E2EE, blocking/bans, membership checks); trust applications (Chat, Scene, VTC, Graph).
3. Governance mapping: ecosystem governance framework in JMAP terms = Space roles/rules, operator federation allow-list, did:webvh witness policy.
4. Credentials gap: how a VC could attach without spec changes (ChatContact/Space role backed by operator-verified VC; trust-registry lookup as operator policy hook via existing fail-open hooks). Each marked deployment pattern, not protocol feature. Reference jmap-did #vc-relationship.
5. Worked example: IETF/ASF/W3C federation, each its own governance authority; trust of a liaison room's membership across them.
6. Non-goals: no DIDComm transport, no mandatory VCs, no trust-registry protocol.

Placement: repo root next to jmap-did-guide.md; add one-sentence link from jmap-did-guide.md.
